title: Letters of Abbess Wendreda
author: Wendreda of the Quiet House
pages: Year Without Dawn, Brightwake. Still no thaw. Little Hild has the cough. The Keeper sends prayers. I would rather she sent grain. I have lit every candle in the abbey and the cold sits under them.
Reaping, that brought no reaping. I have buried four. I keep their candles lit. In the night, beneath the candle-wall, I heard singing with no singers. It said: they need not be cold. It said: give.
Deepnight. Seven graves now. I went down to the singing. I gave my name, and they gave me back my children for one night, quiet and cold and smiling. It was worth it. It was not worth it.
Seventy years since the fire. They believe I died in it. I keep my death in a small place where no one will dig: beside my youngest, under a stone with no name. Let them search the great tombs.
